description: A single-panel X-ray diffraction figure: nine XRD patterns stacked with vertical offsets, plotted as Intensity (cps) on the y-axis (0–10000, ticks every 2000) against 2θ (°) on the x-axis (30–90°, ticks every 10°). A legend at the upper right lists the specimens in offset order from bottom to top: HR (black), 700 °C, 1 h (red), 800 °C, 1 h (blue), 850 °C, 1 h (magenta), 900 °C, 1 h (green), 950 °C, 1 h (dark blue), 1000 °C, 1 h (cyan), 1100 °C, 1 h (purple), 1200 °C, 1 h (light purple/maroon). Every pattern contains strong sharp reflections in the 2θ ≈ 43–45° and 64–66° regions plus further peaks near 74° and 81–82°, and weaker features near 48–50°. Phase markers "α", "γ" and "κ" are printed above the low-temperature patterns (HR to 850 °C), labelling individual reflections. The figure demonstrates that the hot-rolled and all annealed specimens share the same α- and γ-related reflections, whereas κ-carbide reflections are present only in the 700, 800 and 850 °C specimens and are absent from the HR, 900 °C and higher-temperature patterns — i.e. κ-carbide disappears on annealing at or above 900 °C.

observations.observation: The figure is a single XRD panel with nine vertically offset patterns, x-axis 2θ = 30–90° (ticks every 10°) and y-axis Intensity (cps) = 0–10000 (ticks every 2000).
The legend names nine conditions exactly as: '1200°C, 1 h', '1100°C, 1 h', '1000°C, 1 h', '950°C, 1 h', '900°C, 1 h', '850°C, 1 h', '800°C, 1 h', '700°C, 1 h' and 'HR'.
Phase markers labelled α, γ and κ are printed above the lower patterns (HR through 850 °C) at reflections grouped around 2θ ≈ 43–50°, 64–67° and 73–82°.
All nine patterns keep the same strong sharp reflections near 2θ ≈ 43–45° and 64–66° with additional peaks near 74° and 81–82°; no new reflection positions appear at higher annealing temperature.
No numeric 2θ or intensity values are printed on the patterns; peak positions can only be read against the axis gridlines.
The caption states the figure shows 'XRD results of hot rolled and annealed specimens'.
The citing text states that peaks of κ-carbide are seen in the specimens annealed at 700 °C, 800 °C and 850 °C.
The citing text states that no obvious peaks of γ phase can be seen in the specimen annealed at 700 °C.
The citing text states that κ-carbide peaks are not seen in the hot rolled specimen, probably due to the low volume fraction of κ-carbide or the coherency of κ-carbide and α matrix.
The citing text states lattice parameters calculated from the XRD profiles: α phase 2.89–2.91 Å, γ phase 3.65–3.67 Å and κ-carbide 3.76–3.79 Å (values not printed on the figure itself).

Comparison of the 850 °C and 900 °C traces indicates that the κ-related reflections present at 850 °C are no longer visible at 900 °C, matching the reported dissolution of κ-carbide between 850 °C and 900 °C.

subfigures.description: One stacked XRD plot (no (a)/(b) lettering) with nine vertically offset diffractograms of the same Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel: HR and 700–1200 °C/1 h annealed specimens; 2θ = 30–90°, Intensity = 0–10000 cps; α, γ and κ phase markers printed above the low-temperature traces; legend at upper right.

unreadable_items: Exact 2θ positions and intensities of individual reflections are not printed as data labels; only gridline-referenced reading is possible.

The α/γ/κ marker letters are crowded and partly overlapping in the 43–50° region of the low-temperature patterns, so the phase assignment of each individual low-angle reflection is only partially readable.
